topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, connecting practical histopathology observations to the lecture's learning objectives on cancer genetics and transformation.

topics.label: Tumour Virology and Assays of Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumour viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and how cellular transformation is experimentally measured in the laboratory.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Genetics of Oncogenes and Tumour Suppressor Genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional definitions, genetic mechanisms, and cell-cycle pathways distinguishing oncogenes from tumour suppressor genes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Forms of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how defects in DNA repair pathways, replication proofreading, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer.

topics.label: Multi-Step Tumour Progression and Hereditary Predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the progressive accumulation of genetic alterations drives tumour evolution in both sporadic progression models and hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding administrative remarks, reviewing the lecture outcomes and recommending follow-up reading.
